title: A normalized moving four-point path attains the regular-path quartic floor

moving_path.base: Use K1727's A,B,p_0 and vary the lower-radius total probability p; renormalize by v(p)=pA+(1-p)B so X_p has squared radii A/v(p), B/v(p) and unit variance.
moving_path.nonzero_certificate: gcd(17u^3-38u^2+84u-24, 7u^3-18u^2+84u-24)=1 and the integer resultant is 589824000, so kappa_6'(p_0) is nonzero.
moving_path.implicit_motion: Apply the implicit-function theorem in s=sqrt(q). For all sufficiently small s>0 it gives a unique p(s)->p_0 with kappa_6(X_(p(s)))/u(p(s))^(3/2)=(35/3)s, equivalently (35/3)sqrt(q); write this path as p(q).

scope_guard: The strict comparison is asymptotic at weak matched reward inside compact bounded symmetric scalar paths. It is not a finite-strength global ordering and does not address growing support or vanishing defect.
